claims.text: Adding aluminum to a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Aluminum addition will induce in situ formation of a continuous protective Al2O3 scale on the refractory alloy.
An aluminum-poor Nb-based bcc refractory high-entropy alloy forms an oxygen-contaminated diffusion zone under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Al0.5 and Al0.7 composition ranges have been used in aluminum-modified medium-entropy alloys.
An aluminum concentration analogous to the Al0.5-Al0.7 MEA range is suitable for use in the proposed refractory alloy.
The proposed aluminum intervention should improve oxidation behavior during exposure at approximately 800 °C in air for 100 hours.
The aluminum-modified refractory alloy will form a stable, continuous, and adherent Al2O3 surface layer.
Aluminum will oxidize preferentially in the refractory alloy.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The Al2O3 barrier will minimize oxygen ingress into the refractory-alloy substrate.
Reduced oxygen ingress will preserve the alloy's mechanical integrity after high-temperature exposure.
The aluminum-modified alloy will develop a thinner oxygen-contaminated diffusion zone than the untreated alloy.
The aluminum-modified alloy will exhibit lower overall oxygen ingress than the untreated alloy.
The aluminum-modified alloy will retain hardness and Young's modulus better than the untreated alloy after oxidation.
The untreated refractory alloy will suffer significant oxygen contamination and associated mechanical-property degradation under the stated conditions.
A minimum aluminum content is required to form a continuous and robust protective Al2O3 layer.
An aluminum concentration that is too low may fail to produce an effective protective scale.
Aluminum concentration can affect alloy phase stability.
